items.notes: The taxonomy key, associated object types, top-level label and description are authored Taxonomy definition inputs.
All current WordPress taxonomy labels are represented in the labels shard; generated defaults remain a downstream UX behavior, not duplicate controls.
WordPress accepts manage_terms, edit_terms, delete_terms and assign_terms capability strings. Taxonomy owns the mapping; Roles owns capability definitions and grants.
Public, publicly_queryable, hierarchical, show_ui, show_in_menu, show_in_nav_menus, show_tagcloud, show_in_quick_edit and show_admin_column are distinct native registration arguments.
REST registration settings are authored Taxonomy options. Controller selection remains provider-allowlisted rather than arbitrary executable input.
Meta box display/sanitization callbacks are represented as controlled providers, not arbitrary callables.
Rewrite enablement, slug, with_front, hierarchical paths, endpoint mask and query_var are Taxonomy-owned URL definition inputs.
Custom count semantics are a controlled Taxonomy provider seam; computed term counts themselves are runtime state.
The default term structure (name, slug, description) is fully represented as native configuration.
Native sort preserves object-term assignment order when WordPress stores relationships. It is not a general persistent term ordering engine.
The native args property supplies default arguments to object-term retrieval and is retained as bounded expert configuration.
WordPress marks _builtin for internal use. The Bank intentionally retains it as rejected discovery evidence.
Current core documents a maximum 32-character taxonomy key and requires lowercase alphanumeric characters, dashes and underscores. This is save-time validation, not another option.

items.member: reserved query variables and conflict-prone names
items.notes: Reserved/conflicting names must be rejected or diagnosed when validating taxonomy keys/query variables; the validator derives this from authored identity/URL inputs.
Taxonomies must be registered during the supported WordPress lifecycle (normally init). Registration timing is runtime orchestration rather than authored Taxonomy data.

WordPress derives publicly_queryable from public, show_ui from public, show_in_menu/show_tagcloud/show_in_quick_edit from show_ui, show_in_nav_menus from public and query_var/rewrite defaults. WPE should preview effective values without storing duplicate derived options.

items.member: attach an existing taxonomy to an object type
items.notes: Dynamic binding is a runtime mutation of the authored object_types association. It does not create a second relation engine.
Dynamic unbinding is lifecycle behavior around object_types; missing/degraded associations should remain diagnosable rather than silently discarded.

items.member: term creation, parent and uniqueness checks
items.notes: Term values are runtime content. Taxonomy owns term lifecycle semantics but Bank records describe definition configuration, not individual term rows.
Term rename/reparent/slug updates are controlled lifecycle operations rather than persistent Taxonomy-definition settings.

items.member: term deletion, child reparenting, default replacement and term-meta cleanup
items.notes: Deletion removes term metadata/relationships as core specifies, reparents hierarchical children, and can substitute a default term. WPE must expose impact before destructive operations.
Unregistering a taxonomy is a definition lifecycle operation; built-in taxonomies are protected. Disable/delete UX is a workflow over the definition, not a register_taxonomy argument.
Term counts are runtime data maintained through WordPress counting APIs and the configured callback; they are not user-authored Taxonomy options.
When default_term is configured, core ensures the term exists and records its term ID in the default_term_<taxonomy> option. This is materialization of the authored default-term configuration.

items.member: hierarchical versus non-hierarchical default meta boxes
items.notes: Core chooses category-style or tag-style meta box behavior according to hierarchy when no custom provider is supplied.
REST term mutations enforce taxonomy capability semantics and term-meta permissions. WPE must not bypass WordPress capability checks when REST is enabled.

Multisite may deploy one definition across sites, but term content and object-term relationships remain blog/site scoped through the active table prefix. No network-global term-value engine is introduced.

WordPress exposes rewrite/query configuration but does not make conflicting namespaces safe automatically. Collision detection and URL preview are derived validation/diagnostics over existing authored settings.
Taxonomy supplies the taxonomy/term target. Field definitions, validation and term-meta value schema remain owned by Fields.
Taxonomy defines valid taxonomies and terms; connect/disconnect edge semantics and relationship mutation orchestration remain owned by Relations.
Taxonomy exposes definition metadata and default native args; reusable query AST, filtering and saved-query semantics remain owned by Query.
Taxonomy owns the four capability-name mappings used by a taxonomy. Creating capabilities, assigning them to roles/users and role policy remain owned by Roles.
show_admin_column is Taxonomy configuration; arbitrary column definitions, formatting, filtering and editing remain owned by Admin Columns.

items.member: persistent term/content ordering beyond native assignment order
items.notes: Native sort only preserves object-term assignment order. Independent/manual persistent content ordering belongs to Content Order.
Taxonomy supplies term definitions and queryability signals, while generalized indexing, weighting, synonyms and relevance remain owned by Search.
